title: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
notes: The book creates a different kind of tension, which makes it unique in many ways. In most books, the main villain or obstacle is a single person. In The Martian, however, the problem itself acts as the antagonist, and the tension and pacing come from solving that problem and adapting to new ones as they appear. The comedy is also genuinely good and uplifting, even for someone who could die at any moment. I read this book after watching the movie, and I think some scenes work better in the movie because the emotions they convey make more sense in context.

title: Speak
author: Laurie Halse
notes: This book is far from perfect, but I think a lot of people should read it. In my opinion, the ending was perfect because the book focuses on the realism of what someone might have gone through in real life. If you need a reason to read this book, read it to better understand the trauma that someone else in our world has sadly gone through.
